title: Dan's own group in Vancouver and his mother's lyrics
summary: Dan explains how singer-bassist Adam Thomas led to an album of Iola's lyrics to Dave's tunes, recorded live at The Cellar and nearly winning a Juno.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Now I don’t want to read anything into this, but you both have had your own groups and continue to, and like most musicians you wear many hats to create. The music you do © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
when you lead your own groups, do you think you’ve made a conscious or unconscious decision to sort of separate it from the Brubeck heritage?

Well in my group there is the bass player in the group is a singer. And actually the way it happened — very organically because I was playing gigs around Vancouver and I you know was using different people. And someone said, “Oh you should try this bass player.” So this guy Adam Thomas came and played on a gig and he was a great bass player and upright bass. And a couple of gigs in you know when I called him for this and that I called, I think I called “In Your Own Sweet Way” and said, “Do you want me to sing it?” And I was like well this could be horrible or it could be great but there’s, whatever, 30 people out there. Who cares? Just sure, go ahead, sing it. And he just sounded great singing it. And I realized that no one had ever done — taken my mom’s lyrics and you know put together everything — or it wouldn’t be everything but put together like we did a double album where it was all lyrics that my mom had written and songs my dad had written. My mom wrote the lyrics for the tunes my dad wrote. And you know no one had really done that before. So I thought this is a good vehicle to try it. But as far as in that group we often, prior to that project we would just play all kinds of tunes and just you know pick tunes that we liked playing, like you would on a normal jazz gig. So I don’t know that’s a weird way of explaining it but that was the one thing that gave us a direction. And then that kind of took off and we actually got nominated for a Juno and all we literally did was record a concert we did at The Cellar in Vancouver and put it out. And mostly because I wanted those tunes recorded. And it got picked up by the Juno people and they were like this is amazing. So we almost won a Juno. We were in the last three of best jazz records.
